'''Alexei Yuryevich Smirnov''' ({{langx|ru|Алексе́й Ю́рьевич Cмирно́в}}; born October 16, 1951) is a [[neutrino]] physics researcher and one of the discoverers of the [[Mikheyev–Smirnov–Wolfenstein effect|MSW Effect]].

==Education==
Smirnov graduated from [[MSU Faculty of Physics]] of [[Moscow State University]] in 1974. In 1977, he began to work at the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] (INR) of the [[Academy of Sciences of the USSR]], where he received his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in 1979. In 1989, he received a degree of Doctor of Physical and Mathematical sciences. He also taught at the Faculty of Physics of Moscow State University in the period from 1982 to 1990.<ref name="UTAustin-bio">{{cite web|title=The Lawrence C. Biedenharn Endowed Chair in Physics|publisher=Department of Physics, University of Texas at Austin|url=http://web2.ph.utexas.edu/biedenharn/smirnov.html|accessdate=2020-03-15|archive-date=2022-12-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206003048/http://web2.ph.utexas.edu/biedenharn/smirnov.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Smirnov joined the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) in [[Trieste]], [[Italy]] in 1992 as a staff-associate while continuing his affiliation with INR (Moscow) as a leading research scientist. He became a staff member with ICTP in 1997 and where he held the position of principal research scientist.<ref name="UTAustin-bio"/> Since 2015 he is a permanent scientist and Max-Planck Fellow at the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik]] (MPIK) in [[Heidelberg]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexei Smirnov Max-Planck-Fellow am MPIK|date=9 May 2014 |publisher=Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics|language=de|url=https://www.mpi-hd.mpg.de/mpi/en/public-relations/news/news-item/alexei-smirnov-max-planck-fellow-am-mpik|accessdate=2020-03-15}}</ref>

==Research and achievements==
The main area of Smirnov's research is neutrino physics and astrophysics. In 1984—1985, following earlier work by [[Lincoln Wolfenstein]], Smirnov, together with [[Stanislav Mikheyev]], uncovered effects of resonance enhancement of neutrino oscillations in matter<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mikeyev|first1=S.P.|last2=Smirnov|first2=A.Yu.|title=Resonance Amplification of Oscillations in Matter and Spectroscopy of Solar Neutrinos|journal=Yadernaya Fizika|date=1985|volume=42|pages=1441–1448|bibcode = 1985YaFiz..42.1441M }}</ref> and the adiabatic conversion in non-uniform media<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mikeyev|first1=S.P|last2=Smirnov|first2=A.Yu|title=Neutrino Oscillations in an Inhomogeneous Medium: Adiabatic Regime|journal=Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz.|date=1987|volume=92|page=404|bibcode = 1987ZhETF..92..404M }}</ref> known now as the [[Mikheyev–Smirnov–Wolfenstein effect]] (MSW effect).<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mikheyev|first1=S.P.|last2=Smirnov|first2=A.Yu.|title=Resonance Oscillations of Neutrinos in Matter|journal=Sov. Phys. Usp. |volume=30 |issue=9|year=1987 |pages=759–790|bibcode = 1987SvPhU..30..759M |doi = 10.1070/PU1987v030n09ABEH002961 }}</ref> Solutions to the solar neutrino problem based on the MSW effect have been proposed. The effects were also applied to supernova neutrinos and neutrinos of various origins propagating in the Earth.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mikeyev|first1=S.P.|last2=Smirnov|first2=A.Yu.|title=Neutrino Oscillations in a Variable Density Medium and Neutrino Bursts Due to the Gravitational Collapse of Stars|journal=Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz.|date=1986|volume=91|pages=7–13|arxiv = 0706.0454 |bibcode = 1986ZhETF..91....7M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=2018 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2019-06-06}}</ref>

In the following years Smirnov and his colleagues developed a number of aspects of theory and phenomenology of neutrino conversion in various media.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Krastev|first1=P.I.|last2=Smirnov|first2=P.I.|title=Parametric Effects in Neutrino Oscillations|journal=Phys. Lett. B |volume=226 |issue=3–4|year=1989 |pages=341–346|bibcode = 1989PhLB..226..341K |doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(89)91206-9 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Krastev|first1=P.I.|last2=Smirnov|first2=P.I.|title=Spin – flavor conversion and time variations of solar neutrino signals|journal=Z. Phys. C |volume=49 |issue=4|year=1991 |pages=675–681|bibcode=1991ZPhyC..49..675K|doi=10.1007/BF01483584|s2cid=119449106}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Akhmedov|first1=E.Kh.|last2=Krastev|first2=P.I.|last3=Smirnov|first3=A.Yu.|title=Resonant neutrino spin flip transitions in twisting magnetic fields|journal=Z. Phys. C |volume=52 |issue=4|year=1991 |pages=701–709|bibcode=1991ZPhyC..52..701A|doi=10.1007/BF01562347|s2cid=119774437}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Krastev|first1=P.I.|last2=Smirnov|first2=A.Yu.|title=Density perturbations and resonant conversion of neutrinos|journal=Mod. Phys. Lett. A |volume=6 |issue=11|year=1991 |pages=1001–1009|bibcode=1991MPLA....6.1001K|doi=10.1142/S0217732391001056}}</ref> Currently Smirnov is working on implications of the obtained neutrino results for fundamental physics (quark-lepton complementarity, unification, etc.) as well as on future programs of studies in neutrino physics.{{citation needed|date=March 2020}}

Smirnov is a co-recipient of the 2005 [[Bruno Pontecorvo Prize]] "for his prediction and study of the influence of matter on neutrino oscillations".<ref>{{cite web|title=Smirnov Wins 2005 Pontecorvo Prize|url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2006/8/smirnov-wins-2005-pontecorvo-prize.aspx|publisher=Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics|accessdate=2020-03-15|archive-date=2018-07-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704070521/https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2006/8/smirnov-wins-2005-pontecorvo-prize.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>  For his lifetime achievements in physics Smirnov was named [[Alexander von Humboldt|Humboldt]] Research Fellow. This is one of the [[Germany]]'s most prestigious awards in science which enables outstanding scientists and scholars from abroad to spend up to six months at the Humboldt Institute to carry out research on projects of their own choosing.<ref>{{cite web|title=Honours|date=2004-11-01|url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2004/11/honours.aspx|publisher=Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics|accessdate=2020-03-15|archive-date=2018-07-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704072532/https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2004/11/honours.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> Alexei Smirnov and Stanislav Mikheyev were awarded the 2008 [[Sakurai Prize]] "for pioneering and influential work on the enhancement of neutrino oscillations in matter, which is essential to a quantitative understanding of the solar neutrino flux".<ref name="Sakurai">{{cite web|title=2008 J.J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Smirnov&first_nm=Alexei&year=2008|publisher=American Physical Society|accessdate=2020-03-15}}</ref>

Smirnov is an editor of the ''[[Journal of High Energy Physics]]'' and ''[[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]]'' and a divisional associate editor for ''[[Physical Review Letters]]''.<ref name="Sakurai"/> He is also member of the advisory board of  the journal ''Universe''. His awards and honors also include the Biedenharn endowed chair in physics (University of Texas, Austin, 2002),<ref name="UTAustin-bio"/> the award of the Japanese Society for promotion of science (2004), an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] research award (2004), and the [[Erwin Schrödinger]] guest professorship (Vienna, 2007),<ref name="Sakurai"/> as well as the 2016 [[Albert Einstein Medal]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ICTP Physicist Awarded Einstein Medal|url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/2016/2/smirnov_prize.aspx|date=2016-02-03|publisher=Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics|accessdate=2020-03-15}}</ref>
